descriptors.definition: The Securities and Exchange Board of India was established as a statutory body to protect investor interests, promote market development, and regulate securities operations. It prevents market malpractices and consolidates oversight previously scattered across multiple administrative enactments.
inclusion: Regulatory oversight of merchant banks and mutual funds
Supervision of stock exchange activities and new issue processes
exclusion: Non-statutory administrative advisory functions operating prior to 1992
nearby_distinctions: Distinguished from the pre-1992 fragmented regulatory framework by holding unified statutory enforcement powers

descriptors.definition: The statute provides precise legal definitions for entities, collective schemes, and judicial or technical members functioning within the regulatory framework. Undefined expressions default to meanings assigned under connected securities and depository enactments.
inclusion: Definitions of Chairman, Members, and Reserve Bank
Incorporation and management structure provisions
exclusion: Substantive regulatory powers and penalty enforcement mechanisms
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between judicial members, technical members, and general board members

descriptors.concept_name: Establishment and Management of the Board
descriptors.definition: SEBI operates as a corporate body with perpetual succession, a common seal, and the capacity to contract and hold property. Its overall management and superintendence vest in a designated board of members appointed by the Central Government.
inclusion: Head office location at Mumbai
Composition rules including government nominees and RBI representation
Tenure, termination, and resignation conditions
exclusion: Specific market investigation and adjudication powers
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between ex-officio government/RBI nominees and nominated professional members appointed under specific statutory sub-sections

descriptors.definition: The regulatory board holds comprehensive duties to protect investors, develop the securities market, and supervise stock exchanges and market intermediaries. It possesses authority to prohibit fraudulent practices, conduct inspections, and call for relevant information.
inclusion: Registration and working regulations for stockbrokers, merchant bankers, and depositories
Prohibition of fraudulent trade practices and insider trading
Power to call for records from banks and other authorities
exclusion: Direct corporate management execution outside of regulatory oversight
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes between general market development duties and specific investigative and registration mandates

descriptors.concept_name: Regulation of Prospectus and Offer Documents
descriptors.definition: The regulatory board is empowered to specify disclosure norms, capital issuance rules, and listing requirements for companies. It can prohibit public issuance of offer documents or mandate specific conditions for issuing prospectuses to protect investors.
inclusion: Regulation of capital issue matters and transfer of securities
General or special orders prohibiting companies from soliciting money through defective offer documents
exclusion: Routine internal corporate capital restructuring without public solicitation
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes general supervisory powers from specific prohibitions on public capital solicitation offer documents

descriptors.concept_name: Collective Investment Scheme Definition and Exceptions
descriptors.definition: Any arrangement where investor contributions are pooled to receive profits and managed without day-to-day investor control constitutes a collective investment scheme. Unregistered pooling schemes involving a corpus of one hundred crore rupees or more are statutorily deemed collective investment schemes.
inclusion: Arrangements involving pooled contributions for profit generation with professional management
Statutory threshold deeming rules for unregistered large corpuses
exclusion: Schemes offered by registered co-operative societies
Deposit acceptance activities by non-banking financial companies
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes regulated collective investment vehicles from cooperative society activities and NBFC deposit acceptances

descriptors.concept_name: Power to Issue Directions, Levy Penalties, and Disgorge Profits
descriptors.definition: The regulatory board can issue directions, conduct inquiries, and levy statutory penalties against entities violating market regulations. This enforcement authority explicitly incorporates the power to order the disgorgement of wrongful gains made or losses averted.
inclusion: Levying monetary penalties following an inquiry
Recouping unlawful profits or avoided losses from illegal market transactions
exclusion: Standard administrative supervisory reviews lacking inquiry findings
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes corrective administrative directions from punitive monetary fines and profit disgorgement orders

descriptors.definition: When reasonable grounds indicate market detriment or rule violations, the board can order an investigation into intermediaries or associated persons. Investigating authorities can inspect, search, and temporarily retain custody of relevant books and records.
inclusion: Duty of company officers and intermediaries to preserve and produce records
Authority to keep seized documents in custody for up to six months
exclusion: Permanent confiscation of books without statutory return obligations
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes routine information-calling powers from formal investigative search and seizure proceedings

descriptors.definition: The board may issue cease and desist orders against persons violating or likely to violate statutory rules after conducting an inquiry. Listed public companies and prospective issuers are protected from such orders unless there are reasonable grounds indicating insider trading or market manipulation.
inclusion: Orders requiring cessation of violations by market participants
Threshold protections for general public companies regarding non-manipulative operational matters
exclusion: Intermediaries registered under section 12, which lack standard listed company safe harbors against cease and desist actions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes general corporate operations from specific insider trading and market manipulation exceptions applicable to listed companies

descriptors.concept_name: Registration Certificate Requirement for Market Intermediaries
descriptors.definition: Market intermediaries, stock brokers, depositories, and fund sponsors must obtain a certificate of registration from the board before buying, selling, or dealing in securities. The board holds powers to suspend or cancel these registrations following a fair hearing opportunity.
inclusion: Mandatory registration for merchant bankers, underwriters, credit rating agencies, and mutual fund sponsors
Procedural requirements providing a reasonable opportunity of being heard prior to cancellation
exclusion: Unregistered trading operations conducted without valid board certification
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes authorized market participants operating under valid registration certificates from unauthorized entities

descriptors.concept_name: Prohibition of Manipulative Devices, Insider Trading, and Fraud
descriptors.definition: The law prohibits any person from employing manipulative devices, deceptive contrivances, or fraudulent schemes in connection with listed securities. It strictly outlaws insider trading, dealing while possessing non-public information, and unauthorized substantial acquisitions of corporate control.
inclusion: Direct or indirect fraud in securities purchase or sale
Unlawful communication and trading based on material non-public information
Unlawful acquisition of equity shares exceeding specified thresholds
exclusion: Transparent market transactions executed in full compliance with regulatory norms
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes standard portfolio trading from fraudulent artifice, insider communication, and unauthorized control acquisitions

descriptors.concept_name: Finance, Accounts, and Audit Fund Mechanics
descriptors.definition: The board finances its operations through parliamentary grants provided by the Central Government and a dedicated general fund. All regulatory fees, charges, and government grants are credited to this fund to cover employee remuneration and administrative expenses.
inclusion: Credit sources including statutory fees, charges, and government allocations
Application of fund resources towards employee salaries and operational expenses
exclusion: Private commercial revenues unrelated to statutory board functions
nearby_distinctions: Distinguishes direct governmental budgetary grants from internal fee collections credited to the SEBI General Fund
